knowledge_gaps: The proposed mask is history-dependent, not candidate-specific: the candidate enters only through its TF–IDF dot product. Describe it as a recurrent-token history mask unless a separate candidate-dependent gate is implemented.

Masking without renormalization changes both feature selection and residual magnitude. Add a predeclared attenuation-matched control to distinguish token specificity from simply weakening lexical scores.

Reproducibility remains incomplete: resolve the exact incumbent pooling equations, tokenizer and n-gram eligibility, negative sampling with or without replacement, diagnostic feature shapes, checkpoint schedule, and remaining-budget allocation.

Two distinct item IDs need not supply independent evidence. Rare brands, model numbers, copied descriptions, and product variants can satisfy the gate; explicit duplicate and boilerplate controls are needed.

The report replaces the starting learned semantic encoder and auxiliary objective with fixed lexical features. This is a reasonable simplification, but it does not evaluate the original semantic proposal. Originality 4 and potential 7 remain provisional; difficulty 5 depends on demonstrating efficient sparse scoring and predictor parity.

Historical combined_score values lack verified protocol compatibility and per-category outcomes. Predeclare validation-query limits and report paired uncertainty only when existing evaluator outputs permit it; sampled HR@10 cannot establish full-catalog improvement.
